answer.location_description: Small 3x3 square near the top-left corner of the image, rows 1-3, columns 1-3, well away from the central blob.
answer.mechanism: Two groups of first-layer units read the 3x3 patch with opposite signs. The 'large-blob' units (0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 10, 18, 20, 29) are positive on the blob body/ring and also carry very large positive weights on the patch. The 'small-blob' units (5, 6, 9, 14, 15, 21, 24, 27, 30) are positive on the background, negative on the ring region, and carry very large negative weights on the patch. In layer 2, u3 and u10 take positive weights from the first group and negative weights from the second, and both have positive output weights (+67, +74). u6 and u1 have the reverse wiring and negative output weights (-93, -90). A bright patch therefore excites the large-blob pathway, suppresses the small-blob pathway, and pushes the logit toward class 1 (large blob).
answer.evidence: Patch weights in rows 1-3, cols 1-3 are uniformly signed and among the largest in each grid. Unit 4: 93 49 51 / 98 98 72 / 93 94 55. Unit 20: 81 90 93 / 77 78 94 / 52 38 91. Unit 10: 67 85 75 / 93 99 67 / 46 47 91. Unit 5: -82 -72 -57 / -57 -82 -86 / -76 -98 -98. Unit 14: -77 -98 -44 / ... / -72 -82 -54. Units 24, 27, 30 show the same negative pattern. The surrounding weights (row 0, row 4, col 0, col 4) show no such structure, so this is a sharply bounded square. The patch sign always matches the unit's blob-size polarity (positive in units with positive blob/ring weights, negative in units with positive background weights). This consistent alignment across about 18 units is what a learned label-correlated marker looks like. Layer 2: u3 receives 2:84, 4:89, 8:92, 10:94 and 5:-98, 6:-84, 27:-90, with output weight +67. u10 receives 0:87, 1:94, 8:91, 18:89 and 5:-78, 30:-63, with output weight +74.
answer.main_feature: The model compares brightness in the central disk and ring at roughly radius 4-8 px (positive in large-blob units) with the dark ring and background (positive in small-blob units). Bright pixels extending out to that radius mean a large blob.
